CANONICAL_NAME.value: LISP 1.5 (1962) -- the IBM 7090 implementation, machine-readable transcription of the original assembly

VERSION.value: informatimago/lisp-1-5 machine-readable transcription of the 1962 sources

ERA.value: 1962 (body: transcription of the original 7090 assembly sources)

value.lineage: McCarthy's LISP as implemented for the IBM 7090 by Hart, Levin and the MIT group, distributed with the 1962 LISP 1.5 Programmer's Manual. The body here is a machine-readable transcription of the original 7090 assembly listing (lisp15.asm, ~500 KB) together with the LISP-level sources. LISP is the branch that SURVIVED the early list-processing competition; its principal rival IPL-V (Newell, Shaw and Simon at RAND, from 1956) survives in this search only as scanned manuals, with no machine-readable body found -- an asymmetry that is itself evidence about what gets preserved.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: symbolic computation and automatic storage management

value.built_to: evaluate symbolic expressions -- programs as data -- on a machine designed for numeric work, with automatic storage reclamation
value.pressure: 36-bit words, a 6-bit character set, no dynamic memory from the operating system, and symbolic structures whose lifetime the programmer could not track by hand
value.success_means: eval computes the value of an S-expression and the garbage collector reclaims cells without the programmer's help

value.pressure: fixed core, no OS memory management, numeric-oriented hardware
value.failure_condition: the free list exhausts and the collector cannot recover enough cells

cut.note: the famous names (eval/apply, garbage collection, the a-list) are here as 7090 machine code with the mechanisms exposed: marking by sign bit and by a separate bit table, a free list threaded during the sweep, a recursion stack that is itself a root, a cons budget that traps, and an interpreter whose environment is a list searched linearly

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.mechanism: a cons takes the word at $FREE and advances $FREE to that word's decrement (its cdr); the sweep walks free storage top to bottom, and every word whose sign is still plus (unmarked) is linked into a new free list by storing its address into the previously collected word; marked words get their sign restored
organs.output: a fresh cell, or the reconstructed free list
organs.state: $FREE (one word); the list itself lives in the free cells
assumptions: a cell is one 36-bit word holding two 15-bit addresses (car in the address field, cdr in the decrement); the sign bit is free for marking
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: allocation is three instructions; no size classes because every cell is the same size
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: $FREE = 0 -> FROUT -> RECLAM; if the collection recovers fewer than the critical number the run is aborted (*GC 2*)
organs.human_prior: uniform cell size; the 7090 word layout dictates car/cdr as address/decrement

organs.mechanism: MRKLST takes a pointer in IR2: reject if outside LISP storage; if in free storage, complement the word (CLS/STO: the sign bit becomes the mark; TPL exits if already marked), push the cdr on the push-down list, recurse on the car (a loop with an explicit stack), pop the cdr and continue; if in full-word space, set a bit in a separate bit table instead (full words have no spare sign); the stack depth is bounded by the free part of the PDL (MLPDC) and overflow is a fatal *NO PDL* error
organs.output: every reachable free-storage word marked (sign minus) and every reachable full word marked in the bit table
assumptions: marking may run out of stack (the PDL) -- accepted as fatal; no pointer reversal
a word already marked is a shared or circular structure and is not re-entered
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: reachability from roots without any per-cell header; the sign bit and a bit table are the entire mark storage
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: deep lists (long car chains) exhaust the PDL; cdr chains cost stack too (one push per cons)
organs.human_prior: the mark bit is the SIGN of the word, so 'marked' and 'negative' are the same test (TMI); an era-specific trick

organs.mechanism: full-word space (numbers, print names, arrays) cannot carry a mark, so a bit table with one bit per word is zeroed at the start of a collection (A/B), set by MRKLST (bit = address mod 32 in word address/32), set 32 at a time for arrays (MBTT: CAL MONS / ORS), and swept: a table word of all ones skips 32 words at once (ONT MONES), otherwise each clear bit's word is threaded onto the full-word free list
organs.output: the full-word free list FWORDL and the count FWC
assumptions: full-word space is contiguous so address arithmetic gives the bit
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a second heap with different marking cost (no sign bit) shares one collection

organs.mechanism: the collector marks from: the object list (unless a debug/read-in flag says to skip it), TEMLIS -- a list of (begin,,end) full-word ranges that code (mainly the compiler) registers as 'places where list structure may be' -- , then the active part of the push-down list treated as such a range, then every declared array's list elements; a word in a range is marked only if it has no tag/prefix bits (OFT TMPTM), i.e. looks like a pointer
organs.input: the registration lists and the PDL bounds
organs.update: registrations by the mutator; read per collection
assumptions: a full word with prefix/tag bits is not a pointer (conservative-by-tag scanning of the stack and registered ranges)
code that holds pointers elsewhere (index registers) must have registered them or they are lost
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the compiler and machine code can hold pointers in raw storage and still survive a collection
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: an unregistered temporary is a use-after-collect; the design pushes root discipline onto every machine-code author
organs.human_prior: TEMLIS is a manual root registry -- the ancestor of 'GC roots' declarations

organs.mechanism: after the sweep the number of full words and of free cells recovered are each compared with a critical number (CRITWN, the free-storage bound is 16x the full-word one via LGL 4); if either is below, a bad-exit flag is set and the collection ends in error *GC 2* 'NOT ENOUGH WORDS COLLECTED' after printing the counts; totals and cycle counts are accumulated; VERBOS prints per collection
assumptions: a collection that recovers little will be followed immediately by another; aborting early is cheaper than thrashing
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the machine refuses to thrash: near-full memory is reported as a failure, not endured
organs.failure_landscape: the record's own: 'the free list exhausts and the collector cannot recover enough cells'
organs.human_prior: the critical number is a constant, not derived from the allocation rate

organs.mechanism: CONS decrements a 15-bit counter kept as the address field of an instruction (self-modifying: AXT **,4 / SXA CNTR1); when it runs out ARREST reloads it from the high part CNTS or, if the whole count is exhausted and the counter is on (TCOUNT), calls error *F 1* 'CONS COUNTER TRAP' with 8 spare conses reserved to build the error number; SPEAK reads the count as a fixnum; ERRORSET evaluates an expression under a cons limit N and returns F on overrun
organs.input: cons calls; a limit set by COUNT/ERRORSET
organs.state: CNTR1 (low 15 bits, in the instruction), CNTS (rest), CNTST (initial)
assumptions: allocation count is a usable proxy for work done (the era's resource limit)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a runaway evaluation is bounded by memory allocation, not wall time; ERRORSET makes the bound catchable
organs.human_prior: budget in conses rather than in time or in stack depth
organs.source_boundary: the counter code inside CONS and the ARREST/AWHOA/SPEAK routines

organs.mechanism: one stack ($CPPI counter) for every routine: SAVE is called with a parameter word naming how many contiguous cells to save (the first is 'PZE name,,IR4', the return address); it bumps the counter, checks for overflow (NOPDL), stores the parameter word, and jumps INTO a table of CLA/STO pairs at the entry for N so exactly N moves execute; UNSAVE reads the parameter word back off the stack to know how many to restore and where to return
organs.input: a block of cells to preserve
organs.update: per call/return of a recursive routine
assumptions: routines keep their locals in fixed cells (no re-entrancy by design), so recursion is made possible by copying the cells to the stack
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: recursion on a machine with no stack instructions; the same stack is the GC's mark stack and a GC root
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: fixed-size PDL; overflow is a fatal error (NOPDL, *NO PDL* in MRKLST)
organs.human_prior: self-modifying, table-driven block copy: the 7090 idiom for a variable-length move
organs.source_boundary: SAVE, UNSAVE and the END table

organs.human_name: APPLY / APP2 (7203-7360) and EVAL's variable lookup EVP1-EVP12 (7735-7775)
organs.mechanism: APPLY(F,L,A): if car(F) is an atom-marker (-1) go to APP2; LAMBDA -> EVAL(caddr F, nconc(PAIR(cadr F, L), A)) i.e. bind parameters by consing onto the a-list; LABEL -> APPLY(caddr F, L, cons((cadr F . caddr F), A)) i.e. bind the name to the body; FUNARG -> apply with the carried a-list; otherwise APPLY(EVAL(F,A), L, A). APP2 searches the atom's property list for TRACE, SUBR (call machine code via the stored TXL instruction after distributing args) or EXPR (apply the S-expression). EVAL's variable lookup: APVAL on the property list first, then a linear search of the a-list (EVL1: compare caar(J) with E), else error *A 8* UNBOUND VARIABLE
organs.state: $ARG3 (the current a-list) and $ALIST; the PDL for recursion
assumptions: dynamic scope: the a-list at call time is searched; FUNARG is the escape hatch that carries a captured a-list
linear search cost is acceptable; property lists are searched before the a-list
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the interpreter is the paper's metacircular definition transliterated (the REM comments are the M-expressions); machine-code SUBRs and interpreted EXPRs share one calling convention through the property list
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the FUNARG problem is present in exactly the form later named (dynamic a-list vs captured); deep recursion exhausts the PDL
organs.human_prior: McCarthy's apply with the a-list environment; the SUBR/EXPR/FSUBR/FEXPR property-list typing

organs.mechanism: read (function, argument-list) doublets from cards into a buffer until STOP; then for each: reset $ALIST, print a heading, apply, print the answer; an error anywhere unwinds (TERPDL resets the PDL, buffers are cleaned) and continues with the NEXT doublet; the time is printed at start, after read-in, and at the end
organs.state: the doublet buffer, EVQRTS phase switch
assumptions: batch operation: no interaction; an error must not lose the rest of the deck
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a job survives its own errors; the first REPL-like loop, batch form

pressures.condition: the organism's work product is linked structure in a fixed pool of identical cells; structure is shared and cyclic; the organism cannot know when a cell dies; the pool must be recycled or the computation halts
pressures.resource_or_constraint: pool size; a bounded scratch area for whatever reclamation needs (the ancestor's PDL)
pressures.failure_condition: halt on exhaustion with live data still small (a leak), or reclaiming a live cell (corruption)
pressures.world_punishes: both; and thrashing (collecting often for little yield)
pressures.world_rewards: reclamation that is exact from a declared root set and cheap in scratch space
pressures.observable_consequence: cells reclaimed per collection vs live cells; collections per 10^6 conses; corruption detected by a reachability oracle
pressures.vacuity_condition: a pool larger than total allocation (never collect) or acyclic unshared data (reference counts suffice)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: reference counting when the world has no cycles; a world that exposes lifetimes
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given a lifetime oracle must reclaim every dead cell at zero scratch cost; an organism that never reclaims must halt at pool size: the world must separate them and must contain cycles or the pressure is a different one
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: automatic storage reclamation (McCarthy 1960, as coded 1961)

pressures.condition: the reclaimer sees only registered ranges and a stack; any organism component that keeps a pointer elsewhere across an allocation must register the place
pressures.resource_or_constraint: registration cost per temporary; scanning cost per registered word
pressures.failure_condition: a dangling pointer after a collection
pressures.world_punishes: unregistered temporaries (corruption) and over-registration (scan cost, retention)
pressures.world_rewards: a discipline that registers exactly the live temporaries
pressures.observable_consequence: corruptions per collection under a mutator that allocates during computation; scan words per collection
pressures.vacuity_condition: no allocation between taking a pointer and using it
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: register the whole address space (conservative scan)
pressures.cheat_control: a mutator that registers nothing must corrupt on the first collection during a hold; one that registers everything must show the scan cost: if the world cannot see either, the root-declaration pressure is absent
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: root registration for a non-moving collector
